sophia: pushed lumen-slim-v2 (int6) to staging vectors. quick sanity run shows recall@1 drop ~3.7% on shortquery holdout — anyone seen this before?
aj: which holdout + numbers? paste the eval output if you have it.
sophia: running shortquery-v2 (5k holdout). command i used:
```
python eval/embed_eval.py --model lumen-slim-v2 --quant int6 --dataset shortquery-v2 --index hnsw --ef 100
```
raw summary:
```
baseline fp32 (prod-canon): recall@1 = 0.909
this run (int6): recall@1 = 0.872  # -0.037 absolute
recall@5: 0.961 -> 0.945
mrr: 0.78 -> 0.745
```
kai: two quick checks: 1) per-tensor or per-channel quant? 2) did you change preprocessing (l2 norm / whitening)? small ef on HNSW can hide recovery too (ef=100 maybe low).

oliver: also confirm vector pipeline: we flipped to `unit_norm=True` in v2? that would interact with quantization. if baseline was normalized and this run wasn't (or vice versa) that'll explain a lot.
eval-bot: regression-detected: metric=recall@1 delta=-0.037 on dataset=shortquery-v2 vs baseline. severity=medium. ticket=#ML-4521
sophia: thanks — re-ran with per-channel int6 + explicit l2 normalization disabled + HNSW ef=200:
```
python eval/embed_eval.py --model lumen-slim-v2 --quant int6 --quant-mode per-channel --dataset shortquery-v2 --index hnsw --ef 200 --unit-norm False
```
new result: recall@1 = 0.901 (nearly recovers), recall@5 = 0.957
so root cause looks like per-tensor quant + preprocessing mismatch. per-channel quant + index tweaks mostly recover the gap.
aj: nice. plan: 1) set default quant profile for lumen-slim-v2 to per-channel int6, 2) add a unit test in eval harness: run shortquery-v2 smoke and fail if recall@1 delta < -0.02 vs fp32, 3) sweep 10 seeds/nightly to check variance and post full numbers. i'll open the PR for the quant profile + test.
sophia: opening PR now and kicking off 10-seed sweep. will post results tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
